subject: Discovery recap: Observability & evals — next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com>
To: Sana Malik <sana.malik@caresync.com>, Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@caresync.com>

Subject: Discovery recap: Observability & evals — next steps

Hi Sana & Tom,

Great speaking with you both earlier — thanks for the time. Quick recap from our discovery so we're all aligned and to confirm next steps. I've pasted the highlights below and flagged a handful of asks for your team.

Summary of pain points
- Hard to detect prompt regressions across deployed models (no consistent golden prompt set or baseline).
- Limited tracing into generation context (hard to trace user input -> model output path).
- Lack of per-route cost/latency dashboards for multi-model routing.
- Rollout anxiety: no easy guardrails for canary/rollback when model quality drifts.

Current stack
- Frontend/API: Node.js microservices, Kong for ingress.
- Models: mix of hosted OpenAI and one experimental on-prem LLM.
- Observability: Datadog for infra, Mixpanel for product events (no token-level tracing today).

Success criteria (what success looks like in 90 days)
1) Golden prompt sets + automated regression alerts when model outputs degrade against baselines.
2) Token-level latency and cost dashboards per route + model.
3) Tracing hooks that link request -> generated tokens -> downstream logs (SRE can debug regressions).
4) Rollout guardrails: canary thresholds, automatic rollback on quality regressions.

Action items / next steps
- Marissa (me): Share Redwood eval template and a suggested golden prompt starter set (attached). — by EOD Monday.
- CareSync (Sana/Tom): Share any existing golden prompts you have and the network diagram for on-prem LLM access (sensitive; share to secure Drive link).
- Logan (redwood SE): Set up a technical deep-dive to review tracing hooks and integration points (suggest Wed next week).
- Marcus (redwood infra): Draft recommended dashboards (token latency, per-route cost, error rates).

Attachments: redwood_eval_template.xlsx (eval template + golden prompt starter), care_sync_network_diagram.pdf (requested placeholder).

Tentative timeline
- Technical deep-dive: week of Nov 22
- Eval run & baseline collection: 1-2 weeks after deep-dive
- Canary rollout + guardrails: target early Jan (dependent on eval results)

If that all looks correct, we'll schedule the SE deep-dive — Logan, can you propose two 60-min options Wed/Thu next week?

Thanks again,

Marissa Cole

- Golden prompts: we do have ~200 prompts used in production (mix of support templates and billing prompts). I'll share a cleaned subset — anything you recommend excluding?
- Network diagram: attaching a redacted diagram (see attachment). We run an on-prem model behind a bastion and use a VPN for limited egress. We'll share full details in the secure Drive folder.
- Timeline: Nov 22 deep-dive works for us. Prefer Wed 11/24 at 10am PT if available.

Thanks — appreciate the quick reply and the diagram. Re: your questions:

- Golden prompt subset: please start with the 50-75 prompts that are most critical to business-facing flows (billing, triage, escalation). We'll use the eval template to run comparisons; any PII we encounter can be redacted or replaced with synthetic placeholders.
- Data for eval: minimally we need (a) golden prompt + expected output examples, (b) request metadata (route, expected latency SLO), (c) a sample of anonymized request payloads if you have them. We do NOT need customer-identifying fields — feel free to redact.
- Deep-dive: Wed 24 Nov 10:00 PT works for Marissa & Marcus. Logan — can you confirm availability?

Attached: redwood_eval_template.xlsx (starter). I'll also upload a secure Drive folder for detailed network artifacts; send a link to my email and we'll grant access.

Best,
Marissa

On Tue, Nov 16, 2026 at 12:45 PM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com> wrote:
> Attached: redwood_eval_template.xlsx (starter). I'll also upload a secure Drive folder for detailed network artifacts; send a link to my email and we'll grant access.

Thanks — quick technical notes ahead of the deep-dive:

1) Tracing hooks: we'll propose a lightweight SDK snippet that emits a tracing-id with the request and appends token-level metadata to an existing trace/span (Datadog or Zipkin compatible). Ideally you can add the trace-id at the edge (Kong plugin) so downstream services can correlate.

2) Golden prompt regression alerts: Redwood can run batched evals daily against your golden set; we recommend a 3-tier alerting strategy — soft alert at 2% regression, high alert at 5%, auto-blocked rollback at 8% (thresholds configurable).

3) Rollout guardrails: we can implement canary routing by % traffic plus a quality hook (if evals report degradation beyond threshold, traffic automatically shifts back). We'll show a demo of the automated rollback during the SE session.

4) Security note: for on-prem LLMs behind VPN we'll only request anonymized payloads and will provide guidance for HSM/KMS integration for key material if you want Redwood to orchestrate.

I'll send two meeting slots for Wed/Thu; if Wed 11/24 10am PT works I'll lock that in.

— Logan Wright
